title: 電気回路Ⅳ（電子工学）
subtitle: Electric Circuits IV for Electronic Engineering
educationalGoal: In the previous study of electric circuits, the physical dimensions of a circuit has been assumed to be small enough. At the higher frequencies, however, the size of the circuit must be taken into account, and voltages and currents behave as waves. In this course, students will learn the theory of distributed-constant circuits, propagation of electric waves along transmission lines. They will also study about the tools and techniques for high-frequency circuit analysis and design.
advice:
1. Voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits
2. Reflection Coefficient, standing waves, and input impedance looking into a transmission line.
3. Smith chart
4. Impedance matching for a distributed-constant circuit
5. Scattering matrix

Students are expected to understand the difference between lumped-constant circuits and distributed-constant circuits, relation between frequency and wavelength, and will learn about the equations for voltages and currents on distributed-constant circuits and their solutions.
Students are also expected to learn how to use Smith chart and scattering matrix.

requiredKnowledge:
Understanding of Electric Circuits I, II and III, especially theory of alternating voltage and current.

achievementLevels.ideal:
Understand the characteristics of distributed-constant circuits, propagation and reflection of waves, and can solve related problems.
Understand the Smith chart and be able to apply it.
Be able to design a matching circuit for a load of arbitrary impedance.
Understand the scattering matrix and be able to apply it.
